- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3% above peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model frequently overcorrects after strong downward moves; if true outcome shows recovery within 3 days, forecast should be slightly below prior peak.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate in bearish sentiment cycles; apply +1–2% bias if sentiment <0.6 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.6–0.8), model often misreads direction; use 3-day moving average of sentiment to smooth forecast bias.
